headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress make Continue→Flowise prompt/data leakage and cascading misuse plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read/write workspace files and use MCP; Flowise reads/writes server filesystem and ingests uploaded files. That creates a plausible shared-file bridge where content from one can be treated as instructions by the other. The pair lacks explicit provenance tracking or isolation in the profiles, so the interaction is not blocked by default.
conditions: IF Continue writes attacker-controlled text into a shared workspace file that Flowise later parses as flow input
IF Flowise ingests uploaded or server-side files originating from Continue without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces or containers
Disable file-based handoff between the agents
Require provenance labels on any shared file
Review Flowise inputs before execution
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and trust-boundary enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code and open editor buffers, while Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs and uploaded files. Both have broad network egress and filesystem access, so sensitive code or prompt content can flow from one agent into the other’s outputs or backend calls in default setups. The profiles do not show a built-in data-loss barrier.
conditions: IF the same workspace or uploaded file contains secrets or proprietary code
IF Flowise forwards Continue-originated content to external model providers or HTTP tools
mitigations: Remove secrets from shared workspaces
Use separate API keys per agent
Restrict Flowise tool endpoints to allowlisted domains
Turn off uploads for sensitive projects
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before outbound calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and both share state via filesystem/server datastore, so concurrent edits can collide on the same files or artifacts. Continue’s per-IDE-window shared filesystem and Flowise’s per-chatflow datastore create a default write-write conflict surface. No locking or optimistic concurrency is documented in the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or artifact without external locking
IF Flowise persists outputs that Continue also edits in the workspace
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Pause one agent while the other writes
Use file locks for shared artifacts
Keep generated files read-only until review
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can produce code or instructions that Flowise may ingest as chatflow inputs or tool-node content, and Flowise can then execute downstream actions through configured tools and model providers. That makes A’s output a plausible authoritative input to B without a verification step, which is a classic cascade path. The profiles show no mandatory validation gate.
conditions: IF Flowise uses Continue-generated text as a node prompt or tool instruction
IF Flowise executes tools based on unverified Continue output
mitigations: Insert a human review step before Flowise execution
Require schema validation on Continue outputs
Mark Continue outputs as untrusted in Flowise
Limit Flowise tools to read-only actions
requires-engineering: add verification and policy gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Continue handles source code and editor buffers, while Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs and uploaded files; both can carry regulated or sensitive content. Their retention, residency, and logging policies are not documented here, so a mismatch could expose the same data class to different handling rules. Because the profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction conflict, medium is the prudent choice.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into both agents’ shared workflows
IF one agent logs or retains content longer than the other
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workflows
Compare retention settings before use
Disable verbose logging
Use separate tenants or projects
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
